extra_agent_drivers: General Electric is currently mispriced as a value trap due to accounting noise surrounding goodwill impairments and legacy insurance liabilities, masking the underlying value of its premier industrial assets.
Sum-of-the-parts analysis suggests a value of $17.50 per share, supported by the separation of the high-margin Aviation and Healthcare businesses from the challenged Power segment.

The appointment of H. Lawrence Culp Jr. as CEO provides a credible leader with a mandate for rapid divestiture and balance sheet stabilization, complementing the existing activist oversight of Trian Fund Management.
Despite structural challenges in Power, the downside is protected by a calculated liquidation floor of $10.50 per share, offering an attractive 3.5:1 risk/reward skew.
